newsitem.title: UK: UK gov't gives tax break to British film makers.
newsitem.headline: UK gov't gives tax break to British film makers.

text.p: UK Chancellor Gordon Brown moved to boost British cinema on Wednesday with the introduction of tax breaks for domestic film makers.
Brown said production and acquisition costs on British films with budgets of 15 million stg or less would qualify for 100 percent tax write-offs when the film is completed.

Giving his first budget speech, Labour's Brown said the three-year measure would cost 30 million stg. He said the measure should boost the number of British films made and help the UK economy by increasing exports.
"The talents of British film makers can and should, wherever possible, be employed to the benefit of the British economy," Brown said.
